note: Static analysis only, no compile/test run. Segment root frontend/apps/ppt-web/src (lib/, hooks/, contexts/, routes/). The segment is very well-maintained (dense issue-referenced comments from prior review rounds), so both findings are concrete-but-modest severity. Finding 1 (medium): logout's cache purge iterates a hand-maintained allowlist (AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS) whose ad-hoc feature-hook roots are NOT machine-verifiable, and the guard test hardcodes the roots it checks — a drift-prone design that has already leaked per-user/tenant caches across sessions on shared workstations TWICE (queryKeys.ts:352 cites #712 follow-up; queryKeys.ts:388-391 cites the incomplete PR #2650 fix). Finding 2 (low): errorHandler.ts's formatFieldName/formatValidationErrors render validation field labels by Title-casing English snake_case field paths and are NOT routed through i18n, contradicting the module's own i18n contract (errorHandler.ts:7-10) — on sk/cs/de locales validation errors surface English field names.

evidence: logout() (AuthContext.tsx:573-596) purges user-scoped TanStack Query cache by iterating a hand-maintained string allowlist: `for (const root of AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS) queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: [root] })` (AuthContext.tsx:583-585). AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS (queryKeys.ts:354-392) mixes THREE classes of root: (a) the centralized `queryKeys` factory roots, (b) shared @ppt/api-client key-factory roots (meters/reports), and (c) ~13 AD-HOC string roots used directly in feature hooks scattered across the tree (developer, ocr, actionQueue, executionLogs, executionStats, ai-chat, financial, rentals, predictive-maintenance, sentiment, notification-analytics, notification-triggers). Classes (b) and (c) are plain string literals with NO compile-time or lint link back to the query keys actually used at their call sites — nothing forces a new ad-hoc root to be added here.

This is not hypothetical: the file's own comments document TWO prior cross-session data leaks caused by exactly this drift. queryKeys.ts:352 cites issue #712 (logout's original `queryClient.clear()` was replaced by this scoped list); queryKeys.ts:388-391 states the `notification-triggers` root 'leaked into the next session (PR #2650 fix was incomplete - this root was missed)'. The purge covers 'the most sensitive data in the app' (AuthContext.test.tsx:205-208: invoices, contacts, bank statements, payment matching, AR aging) which 'must never survive logout on a shared workstation' (queryKeys.ts:348-350).

The regression guard cannot catch future drift for class (b)/(c) roots: AuthContext.test.tsx:188-217 asserts `expect(AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS).toContain(root)` over a HARD-CODED literal array of roots (user, faults, ai-chat, developer, financial, ...). A newly added ad-hoc feature-hook root must be manually added to BOTH the source list AND this test's literal array; if a developer forgets both (the exact failure mode of #712/#2650), the test still passes green and the new user-/tenant-scoped cache silently survives logout on a shared workstation. Landable pure-frontend hardening: derive the eviction set from a single machine-checkable source (e.g. mark every auth-scoped key factory and enumerate them, or add a lint/type constraint) so the allowlist cannot drift out of sync with the query keys in use, rather than relying on a hand-maintained list + hardcoded test mirror. Severity medium (+2): reachable data-exposure on shared workstations, but conditioned on a future/omitted root + shared-device usage; confidence medium (mechanism and two prior occurrences verified statically from source comments + the test body, not runtime-reproduced today).

errorHandler.ts documents an i18n contract in its header (errorHandler.ts:7-10): user-facing copy 'is resolved through the shared i18n' and only opaque tokens (requestIds, raw backend messages) pass through untranslated. parseApiError honours this by resolving titles/messages via `i18n.t('errors.catalogue.<code>...')` (errorHandler.ts:103,108-117,133). But formatFieldName (errorHandler.ts:437-447) builds a user-facing field LABEL purely from the English field path: it splits the backend snake_case path on '_' and Title-cases each ASCII word (`word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1)`), with no i18n lookup. formatValidationErrors (errorHandler.ts:422-428) then renders `${formatFieldName(field)}: ${message}` for display.

Consequence: the app ships sk/cs/de/en locales (root CLAUDE.md; reality-web messages/), yet inline/summary validation errors surfaced through formatValidationErrors render field labels in English regardless of active locale (e.g. `Street Name: <msg>` on a Slovak form). This directly contradicts the module's stated i18n contract for a class of user-facing text. It is a genuine gap rather than an intentional pass-through: `message` (the backend string) is explicitly called out as untranslated, but the derived field LABEL is generated client-side and could be localized.

Severity low (+1), landable pure-frontend: route field labels through i18n (e.g. `i18n.t('fields.<path>', { defaultValue: formatFieldName(field) })`) so localized label keys win with the current Title-cased output as the English fallback, keeping backward compatibility for unmapped fields. Confidence medium: the missing i18n call and the English-only Title-case transform are code-verified in errorHandler.ts:422-447; the visible impact assumes formatValidationErrors output is rendered to end users on a non-English locale (the function is an exported public helper), not runtime-confirmed against a specific screen.
